catalog_name: Universal Tools Platform - Engine and Tool Implementation Inventory
generated_for: Existing frontend, backend, engine registry and on-demand WASM distribution architecture
design_principles: One reusable engine may implement multiple tools.
Do not create one WASM binary per utility.
Use JavaScript/browser APIs for lightweight or browser-native functionality.
Use backend services only where browser sandbox, external network access, large models or security requirements demand it.
All tool IDs are stable kebab-case identifiers and should be reconciled with the project's existing registry before implementation.

priority_definitions.P2: Specialized engines; implement after demand validation

engines.name: PDF Engine
engines.notes: Validate crate WASM compatibility. Some rendering, OCR, signing and repair workflows may need separate engines or browser APIs.

engines.name: Image Processing Engine
engines.notes: Prefer Canvas/WebCodecs for browser-native decode/encode where appropriate; check format support and licensing.

engines.name: OCR and Document Recognition Engine
engines.notes: Model files are large; distribute separately and lazy-load language packs. Handwriting quality varies.

engines.name: Video Processing Engine
engines.notes: Likely use FFmpeg compiled to WASM or WebCodecs where supported. Codec support, memory and licensing must be documented.

engines.name: Audio Processing Engine
engines.notes: Browser Web Audio API may be better for interactive playback and simple effects.

engines.name: Archive and Compression Engine
engines.notes: Password-protected and proprietary archive formats may have compatibility/licensing constraints.

engines.name: Text Processing Engine
engines.notes: Small text utilities may be simpler and faster as JavaScript; WASM is optional.

engines.name: JSON and Structured Data Engine
engines.notes: A JavaScript implementation is often sufficient; use WASM for large documents or shared Rust parsing.

engines.name: CSV and Delimited Data Engine
engines.notes: Use streaming/chunked parsing for large files; avoid loading whole datasets into memory.

engines.name: Spreadsheet Engine
engines.notes: Complex Excel formulas, macros, charts and pivot tables may not be fully supported.

engines.name: Markup and Configuration Engine
engines.notes: Keep parsers strict and report line/column diagnostics when available.

engines.name: Cryptography and Hashing Engine
engines.notes: Use Web Crypto API for security-sensitive browser cryptography where appropriate. Never claim password storage security from a client-only demo.

engines.name: Encoding and Serialization Engine
engines.notes: Many operations can be native JavaScript; keep one shared implementation contract.

engines.name: Developer Utilities Engine
engines.notes: Use language-specific parsers rather than regex-only transformations for correctness.

engines.name: Code Parsing and Analysis Engine
engines.notes: Sandbox execution must be isolated; do not execute untrusted code in the main page context.

engines.name: Math and Scientific Computation Engine
engines.notes: Define precision, rounding and overflow behavior explicitly.

engines.name: Units and Measurement Engine
engines.notes: Keep conversion factors and unit definitions tested and versioned.

engines.name: General Finance Calculator Engine
engines.notes: Use decimal arithmetic for currency. Currency rates and tax rates require separately sourced, timestamped data.

engines.name: India GST and Tax Rules Engine
engines.notes: Rules must be configuration/data driven, jurisdiction-specific, date-effective and reviewed against official sources. Do not hardcode unverified current rates.

engines.name: Construction Estimation Engine
engines.notes: Expose assumptions, wastage percentages, units and regional defaults to users.

engines.name: Solar and Energy Estimation Engine
engines.notes: Location-specific irradiance, tariff and incentive data should be provided by a separate data service.

engines.name: Date and Time Engine
engines.notes: Use IANA timezone data and handle daylight-saving transitions.

engines.name: Color and Design Engine
engines.notes: Many tools are better implemented in native JavaScript/CSS; image palette extraction can reuse the image engine.

engines.name: SEO Analysis Engine
engines.notes: URL crawling and cross-origin inspection generally require a backend fetch/proxy. Keep static text analysis in browser.

engines.name: Network and HTTP Utilities
engines.notes: Browser sandbox and CORS restrict arbitrary network access. DNS, port scanning, TLS and public IP checks need a backend service; avoid exposing unsafe scanning.

engines.name: QR Code and Barcode Engine
engines.notes: Use image engine for raster export and image preprocessing.

engines.name: Font and Typography Engine
engines.notes: Font conversion and subsetting require careful licensing and format support.

engines.name: E-book Engine
engines.notes: DRM removal is out of scope. Some formats may require separate licensed dependencies.

engines.name: 3D Model and Geometry Engine
engines.notes: Large meshes require streaming/worker processing. Complex CAD conversion is likely a separate native/backend capability.

engines.name: GIS and Geospatial Engine
engines.notes: Coordinate reference systems and geodesic assumptions must be explicit.

engines.name: Office Document Engine
engines.notes: High-fidelity Office rendering may require browser/third-party services; clearly state fidelity limits.

engines.name: Local AI Inference Engine
engines.notes: Model weights are separate large assets. Prefer WebGPU where supported and offer a clear fallback. Never imply private data leaves device if it does.

engines.name: Speech and Voice Engine
engines.notes: Large models and browser memory requirements need explicit download and device checks.

engines.name: Business Operations Calculator Engine
engines.notes: Templates and regional rules should be data-driven. PDF export can reuse the PDF/document engine.

engines.name: Education and Learning Engine
engines.notes: Mostly UI and lightweight logic; use shared math, text and date engines.

engines.name: Productivity and Planning Engine
engines.notes: Use IndexedDB/local storage with explicit export/import and privacy controls.

engines.name: Social Media and Creator Utilities
engines.notes: Avoid platform API dependencies for basic utilities; keep platform constraints configurable and dated.

engines.name: Browser-native Capture and Media Utilities
engines.notes: Use MediaDevices, MediaRecorder, Canvas and browser permissions. No WASM required for core capture.

engines.name: Accessibility Inspection Engine
engines.notes: Current-page DOM audits can run in browser; auditing arbitrary remote sites requires backend crawling.

engines.name: Website Crawler and Audit Service
engines.notes: Not a browser WASM engine. Run server-side with strict SSRF protection, DNS/IP validation, rate limits and crawl limits.

engines.name: Data Visualization Engine
engines.notes: Consider JavaScript chart rendering with Rust/WASM for large-data aggregation.

engines.name: Password and Security Helpers
engines.notes: Use crypto.getRandomValues; do not use Math.random for security-sensitive randomness.

engines.name: Calendar and Scheduling Engine
engines.notes: Reuse date_time engine and preserve timezone information.

engines.name: Label and Print Layout Engine
engines.notes: Reuse QR/barcode and PDF engines; account for print margins and physical dimensions.

engines.name: Email and Communication Utilities
engines.notes: DNS/MX validation requires backend lookup; syntax validation can run in browser.

implementation_rules.bindings: Use the existing project's WASM/JS binding mechanism; otherwise wasm-bindgen
implementation_rules.execution: Run CPU-intensive operations in Web Workers
implementation_rules.large_files: Use chunked/streaming processing where supported; avoid unnecessary copies
implementation_rules.progress: Expose progress for long-running operations where meaningful
implementation_rules.errors: Return structured errors with stable error codes and actionable messages
implementation_rules.testing: Unit tests, WASM build tests, browser integration tests, malformed-input tests and output correctness tests
implementation_rules.security: Validate inputs, pin dependencies, verify artifact hashes, avoid eval/dynamic code execution and use restrictive CSP
implementation_rules.licensing: Review all dependency and codec/model licenses before shipping

build_strategy: Reconcile this catalog against the actual tool registry; do not assume every listed tool already exists.
Group tools by shared engine and identify duplicate capabilities.
Implement and validate one P0 engine end-to-end before scaling.
Build P1 engines in dependency-aware batches.
Implement P2 engines only after verifying tool demand and technical feasibility.
Generate manifests and registry entries from a single source of truth.
Report implemented, partial, unsupported and not-yet-started tools separately.
